reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it explains how users can locate eBay customer service and contact it by phone through the site's support workflow. The displayed support topics, service hours, Call us dialog, phone number, and passcode are presented as ordinary instructional support content rather than a request for payment or unrelated credentials. the available video evidence does not establish whether the displayed number or support process is externally authentic or what happened afterward.

citations.quote: In this tutorial you will learn how to find out what number you need to call and what hours the service you require is available.
On eBay.com, click the Customer Support button. When you are at the Customer Support page, click the Contact Ebay tab.
Click the Call Us button on the right side of the page.
Once you click the call us button, a pop-up window will appear with a phone number you can call and the unique passcode you can use

opening.argument: The presentation links a viewer action to access credentials: the viewer is told to click “Call Us,” then use a phone number and a unique passcode, with the passcode available only briefly. That is a concrete contact-and-verification flow presented as the way to obtain support access. Although no reward is promised, the combination of a required call and expiring code leaves open a low-barrier acquisition or verification scheme, especially because the displayed number's authenticity and what follows the call are not established.

citations.quote: Click the Call Us button on the right side of the page.
Once you click the call us button, a pop-up window will appear with a phone number you can call and the unique passcode you can use
your passcode is only valid for 15 minutes

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense identifies navigation steps, but those steps do not establish that the phone number or passcode is safe, official, or limited to ordinary support. The video specifically pairs a call with a unique, time-limited code, and the evidence does not show the result of using it. Calling the flow instructional therefore describes its format without resolving the risk created by the requested contact and credential use.

citations.quote: Once you click the call us button, a pop-up window will appear with a phone number you can call and the unique passcode you can use
your passcode is only valid for 15 minutes

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited steps show only that the site provides a support workflow; they do not show a reward, asset, payment, or acquisition outcome. A phone number and temporary passcode are described as tools for contacting staff, while the material expressly frames the process around customer questions and purchases. The absence of any demonstrated downstream transaction makes the proposed acquisition theory speculative.

citations.quote: eBay allows customers to contact their staff with questions about the problems they might have while browsing the site or during their purchases.
In this case, using the phone might be the easiest and fastest method.

opening.argument: The strongest warning signals are the direct phone instruction and the unusually short validity period for the passcode. The viewer is told to call a displayed number and use a code that expires in 15 minutes, then repeat the process to obtain another code. That urgency can pressure immediate compliance and is not, by itself, proof of legitimate support. Because the available material does not independently establish the number's authenticity, a deceptive verification flow is not ruled out.

citations.quote: Once you click the call us button, a pop-up window will appear with a phone number you can call and the unique passcode you can use
your passcode is only valid for 15 minutes. Once it expires, you can get a new one by clicking the call button again.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the page's eBay appearance as sufficient context, but a branded-looking support page does not prove that every displayed contact route is authentic. Its own evidence highlights the phone number and passcode while conceding that authenticity and what happened afterward are unknown. The fifteen-minute expiry is a genuine urgency signal that the ordinary tutorial framing does not explain away.

citations.quote: your passcode is only valid for 15 minutes

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Urgency is being inferred from a routine expiration rule, not connected to money, rewards, or loss. The material says the code can be renewed by clicking the call button again, and the stated purpose is to reach customer support about browsing or purchases. Nothing supplied shows that the viewer must pay, surrender an asset, or receive a promised benefit.

citations.quote: Once it expires, you can get a new one by clicking the call button again.
eBay allows customers to contact their staff with questions about the problems they might have while browsing the site or during their purchases.

opening.argument: This is presented as a how-to, but it also actively directs viewers through an external contact pathway: select a topic, click “Call Us,” call the supplied number, and use a temporary passcode. The description additionally invites viewers to visit the publisher's site and other linked channels. That combination can function as promotion for participation in a contact flow rather than neutral explanation. The closest concern is a low-barrier verification or acquisition route, though the evidence does not show a resulting reward.

citations.quote: Don't forget to check out our site http://howtech.tv/ for more free how-to videos!
In this tutorial you will learn how to find out what number you need to call and what hours the service you require is available.
Select the category, that best describes your issue, and then click on the appropriate topic.
Click the Call Us button on the right side of the page.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the material ordinary instruction, but that does not answer its promotional mechanics: viewers are directed to an outside site and led step by step toward a call and passcode. The eBay context may make the route appear trustworthy, while the evidence still does not establish what the supplied contact path does after the call. The instructional role therefore does not eliminate the possibility of deceptive steering.

citations.quote: Don't forget to check out our site http://howtech.tv/ for more free how-to videos!
Once you click the call us button, a pop-up window will appear with a phone number you can call and the unique passcode you can use

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The outside links are explicitly described as a site for more free how-to videos and do not promise money, assets, or returns. The operational instructions remain tied to eBay's customer-support navigation: finding a category, selecting a topic, and contacting staff. The quoted material therefore supports ordinary instruction and leaves the proposed deceptive participation outcome unshown.
